docs.title: Enhanced Quantum Backend Selector
docs.text: Intelligent quantum backend selection for Qiskit circuits using transpilation-based error analysis.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Quantum computing users typically rely on simplistic backend selection methods like least_busy(), which only considers queue depth. This library provides intelligent backend selection by transpiling your circuit to each backend and calculating the actual expected error rates.

Key benefits:

  • Transpilation-Based: Circuits are transpiled to each backend's native gate set
  • Real Error Calculation: Combines the actual gate and readout error rates of the specific qubits the transpiler chose, plus decoherence while they sit idle, into an estimated success probability
  • Multiple Runs: Averages over multiple transpilation runs for stability
  • Fractional Gates Support: Compare standard and fractional-gate versions of a backend (ideal for chemistry circuits)

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
from enhanced_quantum_backend_selector import BackendSelector
from qiskit import QuantumCircuit
from qiskit_ibm_runtime import QiskitRuntimeService

# Get available backends
service = QiskitRuntimeService()
backends = service.backends()

# Create your circuit
qc = QuantumCircuit(3)
qc.h(0)
qc.cx(0, 1)
qc.cx(1, 2)
qc.measure_all()

# Select the best backend
selector = BackendSelector(backends)
best = selector.select_backend(qc)

print(f"Recommended: {best.backend.name}")
print(f"Expected error: {1 - best.score_data.score:.2%}")

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
pip install enhanced-quantum-backend-selector

Or with Poetry:

poetry add enhanced-quantum-backend-selector

docs.title: select_backend
docs.text:
def select_backend(
    self,
    circuit: QuantumCircuit,
    require_compatible: bool = True,
    min_score: float | None = None,
) -> BackendRecommendation

Select the best backend for a circuit.

Parameters:

  • circuit: The quantum circuit to execute
  • require_compatible: Only consider compatible backends (default: True)
  • min_score: Minimum acceptable score (optional)

Returns: BackendRecommendation

Raises:

  • ValueError if the circuit has no qubits or no operations
  • RuntimeError if no backend is compatible or meets min_score

docs.title: BackendRecommendation
docs.text:
Result object containing backend selection details.

@dataclass
class BackendRecommendation:
    backend: BackendV2          # The recommended backend
    score_data: CircuitScore    # Scoring results
    rank: int                   # Position in rankings (1=best)

docs.title: CircuitScore
docs.text:
Scoring results for a backend.

@dataclass
class CircuitScore:
    backend: str                # Backend name
    compatible: bool            # Whether backend can run the circuit
    reasons: list[str]          # Human-readable explanations
    score: float                # Success probability, 0 to 1 (higher is better)
    log_success_probability: float  # ln(success probability), used for ranking

Score interpretation:

  • Score = estimated success probability (ESP), between 0 and 1
  • Incompatible backends have compatible=False and a score of 0
  • Higher scores are better: 0.99 (1% error) is better than 0.95 (5% error)
  • Backends are ranked by log_success_probability, the natural log of the score, which keeps extremely deep circuits apart when every score underflows to 0

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text: Design and implementation of the Enhanced Quantum Backend Selector.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The library implements intelligent backend selection using transpilation-based error estimation. Rather than using generic backend metrics, it transpiles circuits to each backend and calculates the actual expected error rates.

docs.title: BackendSelector
docs.text:
Responsibility: Public API and orchestration

  • Validates inputs
  • Transpiles circuits to each backend
  • Orchestrates parallel backend scoring
  • Ranks backends by scores
  • Returns strongly-typed recommendations

docs.title: CircuitScorer
docs.text:
Responsibility: Score circuits using error analysis

Scoring method:

  1. Multiply (1 - error) for each gate operation in the transpiled circuit
  2. Multiply (1 - readout_error) for each used qubit
  3. Multiply (1 - idle_error) for each used qubit, from its T1/T2 and the time it waits between its first and last operation (as-late-as-possible schedule)
  4. Return the estimated success probability: score = ESP, between 0 and 1

Gates with no reported error use the mean error of that gate across the device, so missing calibration data never makes a backend look better. Missing gate durations and T1/T2 values fall back to device means the same way.

Note: Transpilation happens in BackendSelector, which then passes the transpiled circuit to the scorer.

Multiple runs: BackendSelector averages over 3 transpilation runs for stability.

# Score formula (in CircuitScorer)
esp = prod(1 - gate.error_rate for gate in transpiled_circuit)
esp *= prod(1 - qubit.readout_error for qubit in used_qubits)
esp *= prod(1 - idle_error(qubit.idle_time, qubit.t1, qubit.t2) for qubit in used_qubits)
# idle_error(t, T1, T2) = 1/2 - exp(-t/T1)/6 - exp(-t/T2)/3
score = esp

# Averaging (in BackendSelector)
final_score = mean([score_run1, score_run2, score_run3])

docs.title: Data Flow
docs.text:
1. User calls select_backend(circuit)
2. BackendSelector validates inputs
3. Parallel scoring (ThreadPoolExecutor, 10 workers):
   └─▶ Each backend: Transpile + Calculate error
4. Sort by score (descending)
5. Filter by compatibility and min_score
6. Assign ranks (1 = best)
7. Return BackendRecommendation

docs.title: Parallel Analysis
docs.text:
• Uses ThreadPoolExecutor with max 10 workers
  • Analyzes all backends concurrently

docs.title: Configurable Accuracy
docs.text:
• Default: 3 transpilation runs
  • Configurable: 1 (fast) to 5+ (accurate)

docs.title: Why Transpilation-Based?
docs.text:
Transpiling reveals:

  • Which specific qubits will be used
  • Exact gate decompositions needed
  • Real error rates for actual execution

This is more accurate than generic backend metrics.

docs.title: Why Multiple Runs?
docs.text:
Transpilation can produce different layouts. Averaging provides:

  • More stable scoring
  • Reduced sensitivity to single unlucky transpilations

docs.title: Provider Agnostic
docs.text:
Works with any BackendV2 implementation:

from any_provider import AnyBackendV2
selector = BackendSelector([AnyBackendV2(...)])

docs.title: Chemistry Circuits
docs.text:
VQE and chemistry circuits benefit from fractional gates:

from qiskit.circuit.library import EfficientSU2

# Create chemistry ansatz
ansatz = EfficientSU2(num_qubits=4, reps=2)
ansatz.measure_all()

# Select best backend
rec = selector.select_backend(ansatz)
print(f"Best backend: {rec.backend.name}")
print(f"Expected error: {1 - rec.score_data.score:.2%}")

from qiskit_ibm_runtime import QiskitRuntimeService

service = QiskitRuntimeService()
backends = [
    service.backend('ibm_torino'),
    service.backend('ibm_torino', use_fractional_gates=True),
]

docs.title: VQE Circuit
docs.text:
def create_vqe_circuit(num_qubits=4):
    qc = QuantumCircuit(num_qubits)
    for i in range(num_qubits):
        qc.ry(0.1 * i, i)
    for i in range(num_qubits - 1):
        qc.cx(i, i + 1)
    qc.measure_all()
    return qc

qc = create_vqe_circuit(4)
rec = selector.select_backend(qc)

print(f"Best VQE backend: {rec.backend.name}")
print(f"Expected error: {1 - rec.score_data.score:.4f}")

docs.title: QAOA Circuit
docs.text:
def create_qaoa_circuit(num_qubits=6):
    qc = QuantumCircuit(num_qubits)

    # Initial superposition
    for i in range(num_qubits):
        qc.h(i)

    # Problem Hamiltonian
    edges = [(0, 1), (1, 2), (2, 3), (3, 4), (4, 5), (0, 5)]
    for i, j in edges:
        qc.cx(i, j)
        qc.rz(0.5, j)
        qc.cx(i, j)

    qc.measure_all()
    return qc

qc = create_qaoa_circuit(6)
rec = selector.select_backend(qc)
print(f"Best QAOA backend: {rec.backend.name}")

docs.title: Production Workflow
docs.text:
def production_backend_selection(circuit, backends):
    """Production-ready backend selection with error handling."""
    selector = BackendSelector(backends)

    try:
        rec = selector.select_backend(circuit, require_compatible=True)

        error_pct = (1 - rec.score_data.score) * 100
        if error_pct < 10:
            return rec.backend, "optimal"
        else:
            return rec.backend, "acceptable"

    except RuntimeError as e:
        # No backend can run this circuit; each backend's reasons say why
        print(f"Warning: {e}")
        for rec in selector.rank_backends(circuit):
            print(f"  {rec.backend.name}: {rec.score_data.reasons[0]}")
        return None, "unavailable"

backend, quality = production_backend_selection(qc, backends)
print(f"Selected: {backend.name} (quality: {quality})")

docs.title: Batch Processing
docs.text:
def batch_backend_selection(circuits, backends):
    """Select backends for multiple circuits."""
    selector = BackendSelector(backends)

    results = {}
    for i, circuit in enumerate(circuits):
        rec = selector.select_backend(circuit)
        error_pct = (1 - rec.score_data.score) * 100
        results[f"circuit_{i}"] = {
            "backend": rec.backend.name,
            "score": rec.score_data.score,
            "error_pct": error_pct,
        }
        print(f"Circuit {i}: {rec.backend.name} ({error_pct:.2f}% error)")

    return results

docs.title: Backend Comparison Table
docs.text:
def compare_backends(circuit, backends, top_n=5):
    """Compare top backends for a circuit."""
    selector = BackendSelector(backends)
    recommendations = selector.rank_backends(circuit, top_n=top_n)

    print(f"{'Rank':<6} {'Backend':<25} {'Score':>10} {'Error %':>10}")
    print("-" * 55)

    for rec in recommendations:
        error_pct = (1 - rec.score_data.score) * 100
        print(f"#{rec.rank:<5} {rec.backend.name:<25} "
              f"{rec.score_data.score:>10.4f} {error_pct:>9.2f}%")

compare_backends(qc, backends)

docs.title: 4. Understanding Scores
docs.text:
• Score is the estimated success probability (ESP): the chance the circuit runs without error, between 0 and 1. It is the product of (1 - error) over every gate, every used qubit's readout, and the time each qubit spends idle
  • Higher scores are better: 0.99 (1% error) is better than 0.95 (5% error)

The score is calculated by:

  1. Transpiling your circuit to the backend (optimization level 2)
  2. Multiplying (1 - error) for every gate, readout and idle period in the transpiled circuit
  3. Averaging over multiple transpilation runs (default: 3)

docs.title: User Guide
docs.text: This guide covers all features of the Enhanced Quantum Backend Selector.

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
The library provides intelligent backend selection through transpilation-based error analysis:

  1. Transpiles your circuit to each backend's native gate set
  2. Calculates the total expected error from all gates, readouts and idle time on the qubits used
  3. Averages over multiple transpilation runs for stability (default: 3)
  4. Ranks backends by their actual expected error

docs.title: Basic Usage
docs.text:
from enhanced_quantum_backend_selector import BackendSelector
from qiskit import QuantumCircuit

selector = BackendSelector(backends)
rec = selector.select_backend(circuit)
backend = rec.backend

docs.title: Understanding Scores
docs.text:
The score is based on transpilation-based error estimation:

rec = selector.select_backend(qc)

print(f"Backend: {rec.backend.name}")
print(f"Score: {rec.score_data.score:.3f}")  # Success probability, 0 to 1
print(f"Expected error: {1 - rec.score_data.score:.2%}")

# Human-readable reasons
for reason in rec.score_data.reasons:
    print(f"  • {reason}")

Score interpretation:

  • Score is the estimated success probability (ESP), between 0 and 1: 0.98 means a 98% chance the circuit runs without error
  • Incompatible backends (too few qubits, offline, or transpilation failed) have compatible=False and a score of 0
  • Pass seed= to BackendSelector for reproducible scores
  • Higher scores are better: 0.99 (1% error) is better than 0.95 (5% error)

docs.title: Get Full Rankings
docs.text:
# Get all backends ranked
all_rankings = selector.rank_backends(qc)

for rec in all_rankings:
    print(f"{rec.rank}. {rec.backend.name}: {rec.score_data.score:.3f}")

# Get only top N
top_3 = selector.rank_backends(qc, top_n=3)

docs.title: Minimum Score Filtering
docs.text:
# Require at least a 90% success probability (at most 10% error)
try:
    rec = selector.select_backend(qc, min_score=0.9)
except RuntimeError as e:
    print(f"No backends met threshold: {e}")

docs.title: Compatibility Filtering
docs.text:
# Strict mode (default) - only compatible backends
rec = selector.select_backend(qc, require_compatible=True)

# Lenient mode - include incompatible backends in ranking
rec = selector.select_backend(qc, require_compatible=False)

# Default: 3 runs (balanced)
selector = BackendSelector(backends)

# Fast: 1 run
selector_fast = BackendSelector(backends, transpilation_runs=1)

# Accurate: 5 runs
selector_accurate = BackendSelector(backends, transpilation_runs=5)

docs.title: Fractional Gates for Chemistry
docs.text:
For chemistry and VQE circuits, fractional gates can improve results:

from qiskit_ibm_runtime import QiskitRuntimeService

service = QiskitRuntimeService()

# Include both versions to compare
backends = [
    service.backend('ibm_torino'),
    service.backend('ibm_torino', use_fractional_gates=True),
]

selector = BackendSelector(backends)
rec = selector.select_backend(chemistry_circuit)

docs.title: Parallel Processing
docs.text: Multiple backends are scored in parallel (up to 10 workers) automatically.

docs.title: What to Expect
docs.text:
Transpilation dominates the run time; scoring a transpiled circuit takes milliseconds (about 0.1 s for a 120-qubit QFT with ~46,000 operations). Measured on a 12-core laptop with Qiskit's fake IBM devices (127-156 qubits), seeded, 3 transpilation runs per backend:

Circuit 1 backend 10 backends GHZ, 100 qubits < 0.1 s 0.3 s QFT, 20 qubits < 0.1 s 0.8 s QFT, 60 qubits 1.1 s 4.7 s QFT, 120 qubits 0.7 s 9.4 s EfficientSU2 (full entanglement), 40 qubits x 5 reps 0.7 s 9.7 s

With real IBM backends, add the time to fetch each backend's calibration data and status. Use transpilation_runs=1 when speed matters more than stability.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
The score is an estimate built from the backend's reported calibration data. Keep these in mind when comparing backends:

  • Independent errors only. The success probability multiplies (1 - error) for every gate and readout, assuming errors are independent. Crosstalk and correlated errors are not modelled.
  • Idle error is approximate. Each qubit's idle time (waiting on other qubits, or explicit delays) is charged decoherence from its T1/T2, assuming the circuit is scheduled as late as possible. Dynamical decoupling, which suppresses idle error, is not modelled, so with it enabled idle error is overestimated. Backends that don't report gate durations or T1/T2 get no idle error.
  • Readout counted for every used qubit, even if the circuit doesn't measure it. This matches Estimator-style workloads, which measure all active qubits.
  • Queue time is ignored. The best-scoring backend may have the longest queue.
  • Your transpilation may differ. Backends are scored with optimization_level=2. If you transpile with different settings or your own pass manager, the circuit you run can use different qubits than the one that was scored.
  • Broken couplers. Some devices report gates with an error of 1.0. If the transpiler routes through one, the success probability for that run is effectively zero. On circuits large enough that every run does this, all backends score about 0 and the ranking reflects which backend needs the fewest broken gates, which is a weak signal.
  • Missing calibration data is filled in with the mean error of the same gate on that device; gates with no data anywhere count as error-free and are listed in the score's reasons.
  • Calibration data changes. Scores reflect the calibration at the time of the call. Re-run the selection rather than caching results for long.

docs.title: 1. Handle Exceptions
docs.text:
try:
    rec = selector.select_backend(qc)
except RuntimeError as e:
    # No backend can run the circuit, or none met min_score
    print(f"Selection failed: {e}")

docs.title: 2. Validate Recommendations
docs.text:
rec = selector.select_backend(qc)

# Check error rate
error_pct = (1 - rec.score_data.score) * 100
if error_pct > 10:
    print(f"Warning: {error_pct:.1f}% expected error")

docs.title: 3. Compare Multiple Backends
docs.text:
top_5 = selector.rank_backends(qc, top_n=5)

for rec in top_5:
    error_pct = (1 - rec.score_data.score) * 100
    print(f"#{rec.rank}: {rec.backend.name} - {error_pct:.2f}% error")

docs.title: Example: Production Backend Selection
docs.text:
def select_production_backend(circuit, backends):
    """Select backend with error handling."""
    selector = BackendSelector(backends)

    try:
        rec = selector.select_backend(circuit, require_compatible=True)

        error_pct = (1 - rec.score_data.score) * 100
        if error_pct < 10:
            return rec.backend, "optimal"
        else:
            return rec.backend, "acceptable"

    except RuntimeError as e:
        # No backend can run this circuit; each backend's reasons say why
        print(f"Warning: {e}")
        for rec in selector.rank_backends(circuit):
            print(f"  {rec.backend.name}: {rec.score_data.reasons[0]}")
        return None, "unavailable"
